testName: IISER IAT - Diversity in the Living World (20 Questions) - Version 3

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the International Code of Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN), which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the valid publication of a plant species name?
options: The name must be effectively published in a printed or PDF format
The name must be accompanied by a Latin description or diagnosis
The type specimen must be designated and deposited in a herbarium
The name can be published in any language as long as it follows binomial format
questions.explanation:
Step 1: ICBN requires valid publication to meet several criteria: effective publication (distributed, printed/PDF), Latin or English description/diagnosis since 2012, type specimen designation, and compliance with rank-denoting suffixes.
Step 2: The name CANNOT be published in 'any language' - it must follow strict format with Latin/English description and the name itself must be Latinized.
Why others are wrong: (A) Effective publication is required; (B) Latin/English description is mandatory; (C) Type specimen deposition is essential for valid publication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the taxonomic hierarchy, which category is considered the 'basic unit of classification' and represents a group of organisms that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring?
options: Genus
Species
Family
Order
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Species is defined as a group of actually or potentially interbreeding natural populations which are reproductively isolated from other such groups (Biological Species Concept by Ernst Mayr).
Step 2: Species is considered the basic unit of classification because it represents the fundamental level at which biological diversity is organized and evolution operates.
Why others are wrong: (A) Genus is a group of related species; (C) Family is a group of related genera; (D) Order is a higher category grouping related families.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A prokaryotic organism is discovered with the following characteristics: autotrophic, contains chlorophyll a, has phycobilin pigments, lacks membrane-bound nucleus, and shows oxygenic photosynthesis. It is most likely:
options: A member of Kingdom Protista (Euglena)
A cyanobacterium belonging to Kingdom Monera
A green alga belonging to Kingdom Plantae
A photosynthetic bacterium (purple sulfur bacteria)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics: Prokaryotic (no membrane-bound nucleus) eliminates (A) Euglena and (C) green algae which are eukaryotic.
Step 2: Oxygenic photosynthesis with chlorophyll a and phycobilins is characteristic of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), not purple sulfur bacteria which are anoxygenic.
Step 3: Cyanobacteria belong to Kingdom Monera (prokaryotes).
Why others are wrong: (A) Euglena is eukaryotic, has membrane-bound nucleus; (C) Green algae are eukaryotic; (D) Purple sulfur bacteria are anoxygenic (don't produce O₂).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Five Kingdom classification system proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) is CORRECT?
options: It is based solely on cellular organization (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic)
It considers cell structure, mode of nutrition, and body organization as criteria
It places viruses and lichens in separate kingdoms
It classifies all photosynthetic organisms into a single kingdom Plantae
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Whittaker's Five Kingdom system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) is based on three main criteria:
• Cell structure (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic)
• Mode of nutrition (autotrophic vs heterotrophic)
• Body organization (unicellular vs multicellular)
Step 2: This multi-criteria approach resolved limitations of earlier two-kingdom and three-kingdom systems.
Why others are wrong: (A) Too narrow - nutrition and body organization also considered; (C) Viruses and lichens are not placed in separate kingdoms; (D) Photosynthetic organisms are in Monera (cyanobacteria), Protista (algae), and Plantae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A eukaryotic, unicellular organism is found to be photosynthetic, has a cell wall composed of overlapping silica plates, and stores food as oils. It reproduces asexually and is a major component of phytoplankton. This organism belongs to:
options: Chrysophytes (Diatoms)
Dinoflagellates
Euglenoids
Red algae (Rhodophyta)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Key diagnostic features: Silica cell wall (frustule), food stored as oils, unicellular, photosynthetic, phytoplankton component.
Step 2: These are defining characteristics of Diatoms (Chrysophytes/Bacillariophyceae). Their cell walls (frustules) are made of silica (hydrated silicon dioxide) with intricate patterns.
Why others are wrong: (B) Dinoflagellates have cellulose plates (theca), not silica; (C) Euglenoids lack cell walls, have protein pellicle; (D) Red algae are multicellular (mostly), have cellulose walls with agar/carrageenan.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding the nature of genetic material in infectious agents?
options: Bacteriophage T2 - Double-stranded DNA
Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) - Single-stranded RNA
Viroids - Single-stranded DNA without protein coat
Retroviruses (e.g., HIV) - Single-stranded RNA with reverse transcriptase
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze each pair:
(A) T2 bacteriophage - dsDNA ✓
(B) TMV - ssRNA ✓
(C) Viroids - ssRNA (NOT DNA), protein-free infectious particles
(D) Retroviruses - ssRNA with reverse transcriptase ✓
Step 2: Viroids contain single-stranded RNA, not DNA. This was discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971.
Why others are wrong: (A), (B), and (D) are all correctly matched pairs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A fungus exhibits the following characteristics: coenocytic (multinucleate, aseptate) mycelium, sexual reproduction by formation of zygospores from fusion of two compatible gametangia, and no flagellated stages. It belongs to:
options: Ascomycetes
Basidiomycetes
Phycomycetes (Zygomycetes)
Deuteromycetes
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• Coenocytic mycelium - no septa/cross-walls, continuous cytoplasm with many nuclei
• Zygospores from gametangial fusion - characteristic sexual reproduction
• No flagellated stages - non-motile
Step 2: These are defining features of Phycomycetes/Zygomycetes (e.g., Rhizopus, Mucor, bread molds).
Why others are wrong: (A) Ascomycetes have septate hyphae, produce ascospores in asci; (B) Basidiomycetes have septate hyphae with clamp connections, produce basidiospores; (D) Deuteromycetes are 'imperfect fungi' with only asexual stage known.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about bryophytes is INCORRECT?
options: They are called 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' due to their dependence on water for fertilization
They show heteromorphic alternation of generations with dominant gametophyte and dependent sporophyte
They possess true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) for conduction of water and nutrients
They have rhizoids for attachment instead of true roots with vascular tissue
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, hornworts) are non-vascular plants (avascular).
Step 2: They lack true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem). Conduction occurs through simple tissues and cell-to-cell movement.
Why others are correct: (A) Correct - they need water for flagellated sperm to swim to archegonia; (B) Correct - gametophyte is independent, sporophyte is attached and dependent; (D) Correct - they have rhizoids (unicellular/multicellular) not true roots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the life cycle of a typical fern (Dryopteris), which sequence correctly represents the progression from spore formation to the establishment of a new sporophyte?
options: Sporophyte (2n) → Meiosis → Spores (n) → Germination → Prothallus (n) → Gametes → Fertilization → Zygote (2n) → Embryo → Young Sporophyte
Sporophyte (2n) → Mitosis → Spores (2n) → Germination → Prothallus (2n) → Gametes → Fertilization → Zygote (2n)
Sporophyte (2n) → Meiosis → Spores (2n) → Germination → Prothallus (n) → Gametes → Fertilization → Zygote (n)
Sporophyte (2n) → Mitosis → Spores (n) → Germination → Prothallus (n) → Gametes → Fertilization → Zygote (2n)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Fern life cycle (pteridophyte):
• Sporophyte (2n) - dominant, visible fern plant
• Sporangia on sori undergo meiosis to produce haploid spores (n)
• Spores germinate into prothallus/gametophyte (n) - heart-shaped, independent
• Prothallus produces antheridia (sperm) and archegonia (egg)
• Fertilization forms diploid zygote (2n)
• Zygote develops into embryo and then young sporophyte
Step 2: Option A shows correct sequence with proper ploidy levels and processes.
Why others are wrong: (B) Spores are haploid (n), not diploid; meiosis not mitosis; (C) Spores are haploid (n), not diploid; zygote is diploid (2n); (D) Spores are produced by meiosis, not mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which evolutionary innovation in seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) eliminated the dependence on external water for fertilization, enabling complete colonization of terrestrial habitats?
options: Development of vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
Evolution of heterospory and the seed habit with pollen grains
Formation of dominant sporophyte generation
Development of protective sporopollenin in spore walls
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The key innovation was heterospory (production of two types of spores - microspores and megaspores) leading to:
• Pollen grains - male gametophytes that can be transported by wind/insects without water
• Pollen tube - delivers male gametes directly to egg, no swimming required
• Seeds - protect and nourish embryo, allow dormancy
Step 2: This eliminated the need for external water for fertilization, unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes which require water for flagellated sperm.
Why others are wrong: (A) Vascular tissue helps in conduction but doesn't eliminate water need for fertilization; (C) Dominant sporophyte evolved earlier in pteridophytes; (D) Sporopollenin protects spores but doesn't enable fertilization without water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a comparative study of plant groups, which combination of characteristics distinguishes gymnosperms from both pteridophytes and angiosperms?
options: Vascular tissue present; seeds absent; archegonia present; heterosporous
Vascular tissue present; seeds present; archegonia present; naked ovules
Vascular tissue absent; seeds present; flowers present; double fertilization
Vascular tissue present; seeds present; fruits present; enclosed ovules
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Gymnosperms are characterized by:
• Vascular tissue present (like pteridophytes and angiosperms)
• Seeds present (unlike pteridophytes)
• Naked ovules/seeds (not enclosed in ovary/fruit - unlike angiosperms)
• Archegonia present (retained from pteridophytes, lost in most angiosperms)
• Heterosporous
Step 2: The combination 'seeds present + naked ovules' is unique to gymnosperms.
Why others are wrong: (A) Seeds absent describes pteridophytes; (C) Vascular tissue absent is wrong; flowers and double fertilization are angiosperm features; (D) Fruits and enclosed ovules describe angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student observes a flowering plant with the following characteristics: flower parts in multiples of three, parallel venation in leaves, fibrous root system, and vascular bundles scattered in stem. This plant belongs to:
options: Dicotyledonae (Dicots)
Monocotyledonae (Monocots)
Gymnospermae
Pteridophyta
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• Flower parts in 3 or multiples of 3 - trimerous symmetry
• Parallel venation - typical of monocots
• Fibrous root system - adventitious roots, no taproot
• Scattered vascular bundles - atactostele, no cambium
Step 2: These are all defining features of Monocotyledonae (e.g., grasses, lilies, orchids, palms).
Why others are wrong: (A) Dicots have flower parts in 4/5, reticulate venation, taproot, ring vascular bundles; (C) Gymnosperms don't produce flowers; (D) Pteridophytes don't produce flowers or seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about animal classification is CORRECT?
options: Porifera (sponges) exhibit true tissues and organs but lack body symmetry
Ctenophora (comb jellies) are characterized by cnidocytes and sessile lifestyle
Nematoda (roundworms) are pseudocoelomates with complete digestive tract and bilateral symmetry
Annelida (segmented worms) are acoelomates with metameric segmentation and closed circulatory system
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze each statement:
(A) FALSE - Porifera lack true tissues (cellular level of organization)
(B) FALSE - Ctenophora have colloblasts (lasso cells), not cnidocytes; they are free-swimming
(C) TRUE - Nematoda: pseudocoelomate (false body cavity), complete digestive tract (mouth + anus), bilateral symmetry, triploblastic
(D) FALSE - Annelida are true coelomates (eucoelomates), not acoelomates
Step 2: Only statement C is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The presence of which feature in the embryonic development definitively places an animal in the deuterostome group along with chordates and echinoderms?
options: Radial cleavage and formation of coelom by schizocoely
Spiral cleavage and formation of mouth from blastopore
Radial cleavage and formation of anus from blastopore (deuterostomy)
Determinate cleavage and formation of coelom by enterocoely
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Deuterostomes are characterized by:
• Radial cleavage (indeterminate, regulative)
• Blastopore becomes anus (mouth forms secondarily - 'second mouth')
• Enterocoely (coelom forms from outpocketing of archenteron)
Step 2: The defining feature is radial cleavage + blastopore becoming anus (deuterostomy).
Why others are wrong: (A) Schizocoely is protostome feature; (B) Spiral cleavage and mouth from blastopore are protostome features; (D) Determinate cleavage is protostome feature (mosaic development).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following represents a synapomorphy (shared derived characteristic) that unites all members of Phylum Chordata at some stage of their life cycle?
options: Presence of vertebrae and bony endoskeleton
Presence of notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and pharyngeal slits
Presence of tetrapod limbs and lungs for aerial respiration
Presence of amniotic eggs and internal fertilization
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Synapomorphies of Chordata (present at some life stage in ALL members):
• Notochord - flexible rod for support (replaced by vertebrae in vertebrates)
• Dorsal hollow nerve cord - develops into CNS
• Pharyngeal slits/clefts - modified for various functions
• Post-anal tail
• Endostyle or thyroid gland
Step 2: These features define Chordata and are present even in primitive members (urochordates, cephalochordates).
Why others are wrong: (A) Vertebrae found only in Vertebrata (subphylum), not all chordates; (C) Tetrapod limbs and lungs - not in fish; (D) Amniotic eggs - only in amniotes (reptiles, birds, mammals).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine invertebrate is found to have: calcareous endoskeleton with water vascular system, pentaradial symmetry in adults, and deuterostome development. It belongs to phylum:
options: Cnidaria
Ctenophora
Echinodermata
Hemichordata
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the combination:
• Calcareous endoskeleton - ossicles/spines made of calcium carbonate
• Water vascular system - unique hydraulic system for locomotion, feeding, respiration
• Pentaradial symmetry - five-part radial symmetry in adults
• Deuterostome development - radial cleavage, blastopore becomes anus
Step 2: These are diagnostic features of Echinodermata (starfish, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, brittle stars).
Why others are wrong: (A) Cnidaria have cnidocytes, no endoskeleton or water vascular system; (B) Ctenophora have comb plates, no endoskeleton; (D) Hemichordata have pharyngeal gill slits, not pentaradial symmetry or water vascular system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of class Mammalia that distinguishes it from all other vertebrate classes?
options: Homeothermy (endothermy) and four-chambered heart
Presence of mammary glands and hair/fur
Internal fertilization and presence of vertebrae
Pulmonary respiration and separate sexes
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze each option for uniqueness to mammals:
(A) Homeothermy and 4-chambered heart - also found in birds (Aves)
(B) Mammary glands (milk production) and hair/fur - found ONLY in mammals
(C) Internal fertilization - found in reptiles, birds, mammals; vertebrae - all vertebrates
(D) Pulmonary respiration and separate sexes - found in amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals
Step 2: Only mammary glands and hair are unique synapomorphies of Mammalia.
Why others are wrong: (A), (C), and (D) are shared with other vertebrate classes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the context of biological classification, the term 'New Systematics' or 'Neo-systematics' refers to:
options: Classification based solely on morphological characteristics
Classification based on evolutionary relationships and genetic information along with morphology
The original Linnaean system of hierarchical classification
Classification based only on ecological niche and habitat preferences
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Neo-systematics (New Systematics) was proposed by Julian Huxley (1940).
Step 2: It integrates multiple types of evidence:
• Morphology (traditional)
• Evolutionary relationships (phylogenetics)
• Genetic/molecular data (DNA sequencing, molecular markers)
• Cytology, physiology, biochemistry, behavior
Step 3: This approach aims to reflect true evolutionary (phylogenetic) relationships rather than just similarities.
Why others are wrong: (A) Only morphology is traditional/old systematics; (C) Linnaean system is pre-Darwinian, not neo-systematics; (D) Ecology alone is insufficient for classification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A virus has the following characteristics: enveloped virus with ssRNA genome that uses reverse transcriptase to convert RNA to DNA, which then integrates into host genome. This virus is:
options: A DNA virus using lytic cycle
A retrovirus (e.g., HIV)
A negative-sense RNA virus (e.g., influenza)
A viroid with protein coat
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• ssRNA genome
• Reverse transcriptase - enzyme that synthesizes DNA from RNA template
• DNA integration into host genome - lysogenic/proviral state
• Enveloped
Step 2: These are defining features of Retroviridae (Retroviruses) like HIV, HTLV.
Why others are wrong: (A) DNA viruses don't use reverse transcriptase (except hepadnaviruses which are reverse of retroviruses); (C) Negative-sense RNA viruses don't use reverse transcriptase; they carry RNA-dependent RNA polymerase; (D) Viroids are naked RNA, no protein coat, no reverse transcriptase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which evolutionary trend is observed across the plant kingdom from algae to angiosperms regarding the relative dominance of gametophyte (n) and sporophyte (2n) generations?
options: Progressive increase in gametophyte dominance from algae to angiosperms
Progressive decrease in gametophyte dominance with corresponding increase in sporophyte dominance
Constant equal dominance of both generations across all plant groups
Random fluctuation with no clear evolutionary trend
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evolutionary trend in alternation of generations:
• Algae: Haplontic - gametophyte dominant, sporophyte reduced/absent
• Bryophytes: Gametophyte dominant, sporophyte dependent on gametophyte
• Pteridophytes: Sporophyte dominant (independent), gametophyte reduced (independent prothallus)
• Gymnosperms: Sporophyte highly dominant, gametophyte extremely reduced (within cones)
• Angiosperms: Sporophyte dominant, gametophyte most reduced (embryo sac and pollen - few cells)
Step 2: Clear trend: gametophyte dominance decreases while sporophyte dominance increases through evolution.
Why others are wrong: (A) Opposite of actual trend; (C) Not equal - varies dramatically; (D) Clear directional trend exists.
